newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Bardot backs Le Pen candidate.
newsitem.headline: France's Bardot backs Le Pen candidate.

text.p: Former film star Brigitte Bardot, cleared less than two weeks ago of inciting racial hatred, courted new controversy on Tuesday after pledging support to ultra-rightist Jean-Marie Le Pen's National Front (FN).

The pro-FN daily Present spread on its front page, presumably with Bardot's permission, a hand-written letter in which the 62-year-old former screen sex symbol backed Catherine Megret, FN candidate in a fiercely contested local election at Vitrolles, southern France.

"With you, decency, honesty and sincerity will be the three suckling breasts of Vitrolles," Bardot wrote. The expression "suckling breasts" has been part of French political language since 17th century statesman Maximilien Sully said "ploughing and grazing were the twin suckling breasts of France."
Recalling that Megret, wife of the FN deputy leader Bruno Megret, backed her animal rights campaigns, Bardot wrote: "I support your struggle as I know that you support mine.
FN headquarters issued a statement praising Bardot and saying she was a great French figure.
Officials at the Brigitte Bardot Foundation for animal rights said the ex-actress, who heads and finances the group, had not mentioned the letter to them.

At least one top Foundation official resigned last year in protest against Bardot's outbursts against immigrants from North Africa. Civil rights group sued her last month for writing in a newspaper that France was being invaded by Moslems.
The Paris court cleared her, saying her comments were "above all the expression of rebellion against animal distress made as part of a passionate struggle for animal rights".
The actress says her comments are not racist but motivated by her horror of Moslem ritual sheep-slaughtering.
Bardot's fourth husband, Bernard D'Ormale, is a former FN official but Bardot has long insisted that her political sympathies lay with centre-right President Jacques Chirac.

Her political statements are reported to have resulted in a drop in donations to her animal rights foundation, which has been her main activity, since she suddenly quit the cinema over 20 years ago saying it was a rotten world.
